Scorched Earth: Sherman's March to the Sea

A born and raised son of the south, I studied the Civil War as a serious student for decades. Where I differ from the majority of my southern brethren is my belief that the finest general of the war was General Sherman.

While the other generals were lining up the soldiers to shoot it out in open pastures, Sherman chose instead to wage war against the property, the farms and barns of the southerners. The psychological effect of this resulted in mass desertion of Confederate soldiers, for although they were willing to bravely face the rifles of the Union soldiers, they did so for the purpose of protecting their homes and families. When Sherman was cutting across the south unopposed, burning farms and stealing food, it broke the will of many soldiers.

The Confederate armies shrank due to desertions, and Sherman mopped up the resistance without huge battlefield losses one either side. This was the most brilliant strategic concept of the war.

My adoration of this Union general is due to this: He ended the war by burning barns instead of killing drafted teenage boys. I like that in a warrior. General Lee was pretty good, but General Sherman was the greatest of them all.
